title: POC SME Workshop - Quantization & Prompting Notes
body:
Summary:
This is the living notes doc from the SME workshop on POC model selection, quantization strategies, and prompt/pipeline tuning. Goal of the POC: show a 2x reduction in token cost for our customer's summarization pipeline while keeping ROUGE-L >= 0.92 of baseline and p95 latency under 700ms under typical request/length distribution.

Context / constraints:
- Customer workload: multi-document summarization (3-7 docs, avg 3k tokens total) with user-facing latency SLO 800ms p95, peak concurrency ~60 requests/s on hosted endpoint.
- Security: customer prefers Dedicated but will accept hosted if we can guarantee no sensitive logs leave their project.
- Baseline model: LlamaX-13B (float16) in hosted catalog; baseline p95 latency = 920ms at batch=1, cost = baseline.

Workshop objectives (short):
1) Identify 2-3 model candidates to evaluate for POC (tradeoff cost/quality/latency).
2) Define quantization matrix (4-bit, 8-bit, mixed) and expected memory footprints.
3) Define prompt/pipeline tuning experiments (chunking, summarization templates, reranker).
4) Instrumentation and telemetry to validate quality regressions and cost savings.

Model candidates (notes + quick verdict):
- LlamaX-13B (baseline): best-known quality, heavy memory; use as golden baseline.
  pros: established metrics, good instruction-following. cons: expensive; limited headroom.
- RedMosaic-7B: smaller, newer arch with attention optimizations.
  pros: lower latency, good for int8/4-bit. cons: slightly lower long-form coherence in previous evals; needs prompt engineering.
- OpenOmega-12B: middle ground, better long-context handling.
  pros: strong on multi-doc coherence. cons: larger than 7B, uncertain quantization profile.
- Redwood-Inst-6.9B-QLoRA (fine-tuned): candidate for cheap option if we can run 4-bit with acceptable quality.

Initial selection for runs: RedMosaic-7B (int4/8), OpenOmega-12B (q8 + int8), LlamaX-13B (float16 baseline + int8 experiment).

Quantization strategies to try (matrix):
- Baseline: fp16 (no quant)
- Static INT8 (quantize weights only)
- Dynamic 4-bit (GPTQ-like) with outlier handling (per-channel)
- Mixed precision: key layers in FP16, rest int4/8
- QLoRA-like adapter + 4-bit for fine-tuned variant (if customer needs domain style)

Memory/throughput expectations (rough):
- RedMosaic-7B int4 => fits on 24GB GPU with room for batching 2-4; expected p95 ~250-350ms for 512-token generation
- OpenOmega-12B int8 => needs 48GB or sharded 24GB setup; expected p95 ~450-700ms depending on kv cache behavior
- LlamaX-13B int8 => p95 ~700-900ms (similar to baseline), may get small perf win with kernel optimizations

Prompt & pipeline tuning experiments:
1) Chunking strategy: split docs into 1k chunks with overlap 128 tokens; for each chunk, run summarizer => produce chunk summaries => concat + finalize prompt to produce single summary. Measure quality delta vs single-shot.
2) Template variants: short-instruction vs guided sections (TL;DR + key facts + action items). Prepare 4 template families.
3) Reranking: use cheap embedding model to produce candidate ranking then pick top-2 and run final condense step. Costs more calls; evaluate net latency/cost vs quality uplift.
4) Cache reuse: for repeated users, test KV cache warm-start for similar prompts. Capture cache hit ratio and cost impact.
5) Safety/filters: run quick NER-based redaction pre-stage to avoid hallucinated PII output.

Evaluation datasets & metrics:
- Use customer canonical 250-case eval set + synthetic long-doc suite (50 cases >5k tokens).
- Metrics: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, human preference (small panel), latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, GPU memory, model cost per request ($ estimate).
- Regression threshold: ROUGE-L >= 0.92 * baseline, BERTScore within -0.03, human pref no more than 10% worse than baseline.

Telemetry / infra instrumentation (must capture):
- Per-request: model_id, quant_mode, batch_size, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_latency_ms, model_latency_ms, queue_time_ms, kv_cache_hit(true/false), error_code.
- Per-infrastructure: GPU mem peak, GPU util, CPU pre/post time, number of shards used, cross-node traffic (for sharded setups).
- Quality telemetry: store model output + reference id for offline batch eval; preserve sampling seeds.

Experiment run plan (priority order):
A) Quick sanity tests: RedMosaic-7B int8 vs int4 on 20-case subset (latency, simple rouge). Aim: rule out catastrophic quality drops. (2 days)
B) Full grid: models x quant modes x chunking (small eval) (5 days)
C) Production-like stress test: concurrency 60 req/s with representative token distribution on Dedicated pool (3 days)
D) Human eval + final decision (1 week)

Deployment considerations / notes:
- Dedicated pools: reserve 1-2 x 80GB A40-equivalent nodes for sharded 12B; separate 24GB nodes for 7B int4 experiments.
- Pin model versions in rollout config, enable automatic fallback to baseline (LlamaX-13B) if avg quality drops > threshold or error rate spikes.
- Entrypoint route: /summarize/v1 with feature flags to switch quant_mode and chunking. Keep sampling deterministic for easier diffs.

Risk log & mitigations:
- Risk: 4-bit causes token-level hallucinations on long-contexts. Mitigation: prefer mixed precision for attention layers; add stronger post-filtering + reranker.
- Risk: sharded int8 cross-node traffic increases p95. Mitigation: prioritize single-node int4 for 7B family or ensure colocated sharding + NVLink.
- Risk: human evaluation mismatch. Mitigation: run small blind A/B with customer SMEs early.

Open questions / decisions needed from customer:
- Acceptable cost savings threshold (target = 2x)? Customer to confirm.
- Will they allow short-term log retention for offline eval set?
- Are there regulatory constraints requiring on-prem only? If yes, adjust infra plan.

Action items (owner -> due):
- Evan: spin up RedMosaic-7B int8/int4 images and run sanity tests on subset. (due 2026-02-20)
- Priya: assemble 250-case eval bundle + long-doc suite and label baseline outputs. (due 2026-02-18)
- Liam: implement telemetry hooks (kv_cache hit, model metadata). (due 2026-02-25)
- Jordan: draft deployment proposal for Dedicated pool sizing and fallback policy. (due 2026-02-22)

Notes to self / miscellaneous:
- Try mixed-precision attention (FP16) + int4 for feedforward layers; anecdotal improvements seen in internal tests.
- Keep random seeds and sampling params in results metadata.
- If QLoRA adapter used, measure fine-tuning cost vs quality uplift - sometimes cheaper than bigger model.

Appendix: quick command snippets to reproduce locally (approx):
- run-bench: ./bench --model RedMosaic-7B --quant int4 --input eval-set.json --batch 1 --trace
- eval: python eval_rouge.py --preds results.json --refs customer_refs.json

Next sync: Wed 2026-02-14 10:00 PT (internal) to review first sanity runs.

End of notes.
